notes.meaning: Believers are told to strip off evil habits like dirty clothes. Bad attitudes such as ill will, pretending to be something you are not, jealousy, and harmful gossip ruin our love for one another. A person cannot hold onto these sins and still welcome God's word into their heart.

Just as a healthy newborn baby hungers eagerly for its mother's milk, Christians should long for the pure teaching of God's word. This spiritual food feeds the soul without trickery or falsehood. Taking it in helps believers grow strong in faith and holiness.

Believers have already experienced the genuine kindness and mercy of Jesus Christ for themselves. Tasting His goodness gives them an appetite to know Him even better. This personal experience makes them want more of His word every day.

Coming to Jesus means trusting in Him through faith. He is called a living stone because He has life in Himself, rose from the dead, and gives life to His people. Even though most people in the world despise and reject Him, God chose Him and values Him above all else.

When people trust in Christ, they receive His life and become living stones built together into God's new temple. Every Christian belongs to a holy priesthood, able to draw near to God directly through Jesus. Believers offer up spiritual sacrifices like prayers, praise, and everyday obedience, which God gladly accepts because of Christ.

Peter quotes the prophet Isaiah to show that God promised long ago to set Jesus as the foundation of His people. A cornerstone holds the whole building together and keeps it steady. Anyone who places their complete trust in Him will never be disappointed or ruined.

True believers see Jesus as their greatest treasure and share in His honor. Those who refuse to believe might push Him aside, but their rejection does not change God's plan. God has still made Jesus the head of the whole spiritual building.

For people who refuse to obey God's message, Jesus becomes like a rock in the road that causes them to trip and fall. Their stubborn unbelief leads directly to their own ruin. God has fixed the rule that everyone who rejects His truth will face judgment.

differ.view: Methodists teach that God appointed the punishment of stumbling for those who disobey, but never appointed or forced them to sin.
Reformed Christians believe God's eternal decree determined both the stumbling and the condemnation of those who reject the word.

notes.meaning: Peter gathers the great titles given to ancient Israel and applies them to all who follow Jesus. Believers are chosen by God, set apart as a holy group, and owned by Him as His special treasure. God rescued them from the darkness of sin so that their words and lives would show others how wonderful He is.

differ.view: Reformed Christians teach that every believer is equally a priest before God, with direct access to Him and no need for an earthly priesthood.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholics teach that while all Christians share in a common priesthood, Christ also established an ordained ministerial priesthood distinct from the laity.

notes.meaning: Peter quotes the prophet Hosea to remind Christians of how much their condition has changed. Before coming to Christ, they were scattered outsiders who lived without knowing God's forgiveness. Now, purely by God's unearned kindness, they have been gathered into His family.

Christians are temporary travelers on earth because their true home is in heaven. Because this world is not their lasting home, they must steer clear of selfish and sinful desires. These fleshly passions actively fight against a person's spiritual life and peace.

Believers should live so purely that even their enemies cannot find anything truly wrong with their lives. Unbelievers often spread rumors against Christians, but seeing real kindness and honesty can break down their prejudice. When God touches their hearts with His grace, those same critics will praise God for what they observed.

Christians are told to obey lawful civil authorities out of reverence for the Lord Jesus. Earthly rulers are put in place under God's providence to keep order, punish crimes, and protect those who do good. Submitting to them honors Christ, unless a ruler demands something that breaks God's commands.

God wants His people to answer false charges through the quiet proof of a good life. Many critics attack Christians out of pure ignorance about what the gospel really teaches. Living honorably stops their mouths far better than angry arguments ever could.

Christ sets believers free from the guilt of sin and the fear of death. Yet this liberty is never an excuse to break laws or act selfishly. Real Christian freedom means joyfully serving God and doing what is right.

Peter gives four clear rules for daily living. Believers must show respect to every human being, reserve special love for fellow Christians, and revere God with the deepest awe. Rulers should also be honored properly, but God alone receives our worship.

Household servants and workers are urged to respect and obey those in authority over them. This duty applies not just when masters are kind and fair, but also when they are harsh and unreasonable. A Christian's respectful conduct does not depend on whether the person in charge behaves well.

Taking punishment patiently when one has done wrong deserves no special credit, because the discipline is fair. However, patiently bearing pain when one has done nothing wrong pleases God greatly. Enduring unfair treatment out of a sincere desire to honor the Lord displays the true power of His grace.

Christians are called to expect hardships and to bear unfair treatment with patience. Jesus Himself suffered innocently on our behalf, showing us exactly how to respond under trial. Like a teacher who writes a copy line for a student to trace, He left His life as a pattern for us to follow.

Jesus was entirely innocent and never spoke a dishonest or deceitful word. When people threw insults at Him, He did not insult them back, and while He was tortured, He made no threats of revenge. Instead, He placed Himself and His cause completely into the hands of God the Father, who judges righteously.

Christ's death was far more than an example; He took the punishment our sins deserved upon the cross as our substitute. Because He bore that penalty, believers are freed from the power of sin so they can live doing what pleases God. Through the wounds and bruises He suffered, our souls are rescued and healed from the deadly disease of sin.

differ.view: Pentecostals teach that Christ's atonement provides physical healing for the body as well as spiritual healing from sin, as a privilege for believers.
Reformed Christians believe the healing in this passage refers specifically to the forgiveness and cleansing of the soul from sin, while physical healing is not guaranteed in this life.

notes.meaning: Sinners were once like lost sheep that wandered away from safety into grave danger. Through the gospel, believers have now been brought back to Jesus Christ, who lovingly guides and watches over them. As the caring Shepherd and Overseer of their souls, He protects and provides for His flock at all times.
